C1.rationale: Level 2: Multimodal communication across verbal, written, hand sketching, technical drafting, physical modelling, and digital presentations embedded throughout the design studio sequence.
evidenceLines: Communicate design ideas, processes, interpretations, and environmental and material strategies using diverse communication methods, including verbal, written, visual, and digital media.
Communicate architectural concepts and resolved design proposals through hand sketches, formal and technical drawings, physical models and digital representations.
Demonstrate a capacity for self-direction, effective collaboration, and critical reflection.

C2.rationale: Level 2: Rigorous evaluative critique of architectural propositions against social sustainability, ethical awareness, cultural safety (connection to Country), and building regulatory codes.
evidenceLines: Engage with social sustainability by applying culturally and ethically informed awareness to architectural design, thereby fostering resilient communities and promoting equity and inclusivity.
Apply knowledge of social, ethical, environmental concerns and regulatory requirements to the architectural design process and its outputs.
Implement an iterative and reflective architectural design process based on site analysis and research, the interpretation of the design brief, and the study of architectural precedents.

C3.rationale: Level 2: Integration of digital design strategies, computational modelling tools, and building physics simulation software (lighting, acoustics, and thermal comfort) into architectural studio practice.
evidenceLines: Apply innovative digital strategies to drive and embrace transformative changes in architectural design practice.
The employment and interface of relevant computational tools and analogue skills will be assessed alongside the final design outcomes.
Our curriculum seamlessly integrates environmental sustainability, construction principles, and digital design to equip you with the skills to create adaptive and resilient built environments.

C4.rationale: Level 3: Multi-year architectural design studio sequence culminating in ARCH1302 (12 UOC), requiring technical resolution of complex programmatic, spatial, environmental, and material variables into an integrated architectural design solution.
evidenceLines: In Architectural Design Studio 6, as the final studio of the undergraduate degree, you will develop a single architectural proposal to a detailed level of programmatic, spatial and material complexity. In doing so, you will focus on how architectural thinking and production is influenced by multiple environmental, technological and social factors.
From this strategy you will develop your proposal, or part of the proposal, to a detailed technical resolution.
Apply innovative, rigorous design methodologies that respond to a given brief and site conditions, and address architectural challenges at various scales.

C5.rationale: Level 2: Structured empirical investigation including complex site analysis, architectural precedent studies, and building science data collection (indoor environmental quality and thermal comfort).
evidenceLines: You will research, analyse and interpret the physical and cultural content of a complex site to generate an architectural design strategy.

Architectural Science and Building Environment focuses on applying the principles of acoustics, lighting and comfort to achieve indoor environmental quality (IEQ) and enhanced environmental performance. The course contextualises the science of acoustics, lighting and comfort within architectural design with an emphasis on environmental data collection, analysis and application to optimise IEQ and environmental performance.
You will explore the role of architectural design in mitigating indoor and outdoor thermal comfort impacts through real-world case-studies and online tools.

W1.rationale: Level 2: Compliance with professional architectural practice expectations, statutory planning frameworks, and the National Construction Code (NCC) buildability benchmarks.
evidenceLines: Integrate principles and technical knowledge of environmental sustainability, construction techniques, and regulatory frameworks to inform and enhance architectural design.
Planning frameworks and environmental benchmarks will guide your design thinking, while key aspects of the National Construction Code will inform your understanding of buildability and compliance.
You will engage with industry professionals and real-world projects and develop the ability to navigate design processes, construction methods, and professional legal and social responsibilities.

W2.rationale: Level 3: Studio-based authentic assessment regime where complex urban design briefs, physical model prototypes, and detailed technical drawings are evaluated against professional standards.
evidenceLines: The program structure, with studio-based learning at its core, allows you to explore architectural design through hands-on projects and interdisciplinary learning activities.

You will be assessed in relation to the resolution, coherence and imagination evident in your final design solution, as well as evidence of consistent application of thought, consideration and understanding.
Studio projects will expose you to the complexities of contemporary practice, preparing you to work effectively in teams and respond to environmental and social considerations.

W3.rationale: Level 2: Direct studio engagement with industry practitioners, visiting critics, and practice-based simulated design briefs throughout the core sequence.
evidenceLines: A strength of the program is its focus on architecture in practice. You will engage with industry professionals and real-world projects and develop the ability to navigate design processes, construction methods, and professional legal and social responsibilities.
In Architectural Design Studio 2, you will develop an architectural proposition that thoughtfully responds to place, materiality, and spatial experience.

G1.rationale: A 144 UOC undergraduate bachelor program structured around foundational studio, history/theory, and building science sequences.
evidenceLines: - **Total Units / Units of Credit (UOC)**: 144
The Bachelor of Architectural Studies at UNSW is focused on the evolving and interrelated challenges of architecture, urbanism, and environmental sustainability.

G2.rationale: AQF Level 7 degree providing accredited pre-professional preparation for the Master of Architecture and professional registration.
evidenceLines: - **AQF Level**: Level 7

Upon completing this degree, you will be equipped for diverse career pathways in architecture and related design-based industries or you may continue your studies in the accredited UNSW Master of Architecture program, which is a pathway to professional registration.

ambiguities: C4: Scored at Level 3 due to the high programmatic, spatial, and technical resolution required in the 12 UOC capstone Architectural Design Studio 6 (ARCH1302).
W3: Scored at Level 2 as studio learning integrates industry practitioner feedback and real-world briefs, but external workplace placement is not a universal mandatory hurdle.
